The range of $\theta =\operatorname{arccos}⁡x$ is given by

$$
{0}^{∘}\le \theta \le {180}^{∘}.
$$

Note that the angle $\theta $ spans the first and second quadrants.

Since $-\frac{1}{2}$ is negative, our answer is an angle that lies in the second quadrant, where cosine is negative.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13964047/assets/ca39c4cde40b99fd40a11746a31398d82814268b2df706e3101ee88648c9e2d4.png)

From the values in the second quadrant, we see that

$$
cos\,({120}^{∘})=-\frac{1}{2}.
$$

Therefore,

$$
arccos\,(-\frac{1}{2})={120}^{∘}.
$$
